problem: Prior map-prediction work for navigation mostly completes geometric occupancy or single-object semantics, so it cannot provide room-level semantic priors (e.g., where the bedroom or kitchen likely is) over large unexplored regions. Deterministic completion methods also give no probabilistic estimate for a queried target.
motivation: A robot that anticipates that an unknown region is likely a bedroom, or that a corridor connects to other rooms, can plan target-driven exploration more efficiently. Standard supervision on observed pixels only teaches the model to copy what it sees, so a supervision scheme focused on unknown regions is needed.
key_idea: Train a PSPNet-style BEV encoder-decoder with supervision restricted to unexplored pixels (mask-constrained), so it outputs a completed room-level semantic map plus a probability heatmap for a queried target room category.
insight: Computing the loss only on unexplored pixels is decisive: the observed-only supervised PSPNet baseline gets 25.5% FWIoU, 26.3% PA and 12.6% SC, while mask-constrained SemSight gets 69.3% FWIoU, 86.1% PA and 64.8% SC. Large rooms (bedroom, living room) are predicted better than small ones (kitchen, bathroom), suggesting the model uses long-range layout context. Using the predicted heatmaps to guide frontier exploration cut search steps from 57.8 to 33.7 in the paper's closed-loop simulation.
method: Data formulation: run frontier-based exploration on 2,000 RPLAN floorplans (200 steps each, ~40,000 observation/global-map pairs), with 10 semantic channels (7 room classes, walls, entrance doors, outside).
Observation input: 4 structural channels (robot position, trajectory history, obstacle mask, explored mask) plus C semantic channels of the local map, giving a 14-channel BEV input.
Network: ResNet50 encoder + PSPNet decoder (MMSegmentation), outputting a completed global semantic map and a query-conditioned target probability map.
Multi-task loss: weighted sum of class-weighted BCE on the global semantic map and BCE on the target-class map (lambda_global, lambda_area).
Mask-constrained supervision: the GT is multiplied by (1 - explored mask) so only unexplored pixels contribute to the loss, which prevents trivial copying.
Navigation integration: predicted target probability maps guide frontier-based exploration toward the queried functional region.

setting.backbone: ResNet50 encoder + PSPNet decoder (trained from scratch on the constructed dataset)
setting.training_data: Self-built dataset from RPLAN residential floorplans: 2,000 layouts, frontier-exploration simulated, ~40,000 (observation, complete semantic map) pairs; training uses the first 10 frames per sequence (Method section says 20 stored)
setting.observation: Top-down BEV maps: position, trajectory, explored mask, obstacle mask, local semantic map (10 channels)
setting.action_space: Frontier-based exploration on a 2D BEV grid with fixed pixel step length
setting.privileged: Semantic observation channels come directly from the ground-truth floorplan annotations (local semantic map given as input); no other privileged info reported

numbers.extra: Custom RPLAN-based simulated exploration dataset; task is reaching a functional region, not an object; same step length in both strategies
numbers.evidence: Table 2: Navigation performance under two exploration strategies, w/ SemSight row

numbers.extra: Metrics computed within unexplored regions; bedroom/living room/kitchen/bathroom F1 from Table 1

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmarks reported; only a custom simulation. The split name 'val' is assumed, since the paper does not state the evaluation split explicitly.
results: SemSight reaches 69.3% FWIoU, 86.1% PA and 64.8% SC on unexplored regions, far above the observed-only supervised PSPNet baseline (25.5/26.3/12.6). In closed-loop navigation, steps drop from 57.8 to 33.7, exploration ratio from 17.9 to 14.9, and SPL rises from 53.7 to 62.4.
limitations: Evaluated only in a simulated 2D setting on RPLAN residential floorplans with GT semantic observations; no real-robot tests and no standard benchmarks (Habitat, etc.)
Only the two-strategy navigation comparison; no comparison with other prediction or ObjectNav methods, and small rooms are predicted poorly (kitchen and bathroom F1 ~65-70%)
The paper reports no ablations beyond the supervision-mask comparison, and the 'probabilistic' outputs are not evaluated for calibration
